utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. You will have realised we are late starting because the trial this morning was late finishing in the morning, and we had to allow time for the tapes to be turned over. Good afternoon to the witness. I remind you that the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours, good day, Mr. M-092. Before I continue this sequence of questions that I interrupted at the end of the day yesterday I will ask you a general question to see whether I'm right about that. Tell me whether among the Albanian people there is a custom that family members help one another and support one another?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends. It depends on the family. Sometimes brothers may have good relations, sometimes not. It depends. That is my answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you remember, we spoke yesterday about your return from Stenkovac to Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that you took your own car. If I remember well, it was a red colour that you came to the Bit Pazar locality in Skopje; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was Golf I, a red colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you stated that you waited there for the -- for Isa Zendeli; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you described yesterday, if I understand stood that well, of two of you together took the same road and in the same way arrived to Ljuboten. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask that we move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You took the route across the fields in order to avoid meeting the police; is it so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that you never had any problems with the police. You were never arrested, you never were involved in any illegal activities so that you would be afraid of the police; isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I never had any problems with the police, but at the police check-point, they held us up for over 30 minutes, and our objective was to bring our families to Skopje as soon as we possibly could.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you were in a hurry to take your families to Skopje. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Skopje, there wouldn't be any problems for your families because the Albanians live the free life in Skopje. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until then, when things started on Friday, life was the same in Ljuboten as well for us. We were free to move, to do our daily routine. But in light of the fact that we were surrounded, we felt insecure and so we wanted to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As soon as you arrived at the village, you went to the premises of the crisis committee; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's called the local staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Other people from Ljuboten also gathered there at a meeting to review the situation and see what they would do; is it so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I walked those two kilometres and we saw a large number of police on the site of Radishan, and therefore I didn't go home, but headed for the local staff or community, wanting to find out from them what to do with our families, whether we should take the families out or leave them where they were. They told us to calm down, there was nothing to worry about and that we should remain at home. This is what I learned from the local community.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can I remind you in that meeting besides you, your relative, then there were also Afet Zendeli, Hisni Murseli, Fatmir Kamberi and his brother, Rami Jusufi, Kenan Salievski, Baki Halimi, Adnan Murseli and others; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw only (redacted), Afet Zendeli, Qenan Saliu and Hisni Murseli. Those were the persons that I saw at that moment there. And this is -- these were the persons that assured me to remain at home, not to get panicky, that the situation was calming down and there would be no crisis anymore in Macedonia and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Perhaps there needs to be a redaction as to a relationship that is listed on 7, page 7 line 2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I would like to ask that we move into private briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Witness, that, in the village there was a tangible tension because of the fact that that incident, the mining incident took place and that eight members of the army were killed. Out of them two were from the neighbouring village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not clear about the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated yesterday that you have heard that the mine incident took place at the Ljubotenski Bacila locality and that the mines placed there killed several persons. As far as I remember, you stated that you saw yourself some smoke and that some people who called you on the phone told you that some incident has occurred. So my question is now: Is it correct that because of the knowledge that not far from the village at the Ljubotenski Bacila locality a terrorist attack took place in the course of which eight persons were killed and two of them were from the neighbouring village of Ljubanci. That fact created tension and fear in the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That occurred at Bacila as you are saying. But with respect to that incident, we -- we saw the smoke. This is a fact. It was near our village, but the people at this local staff wanted to calm us, so we don't know anything more about what you are putting to me. Only later on we heard that the two people who were killed were from Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on that date three armed NLA members entered the village who participated in the placing of the mine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This has got nothing to do with the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the crisis committee decided to establish check-points; one of them was near the house or by the house of Qani Jashari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to state to the Prosecutor of this Tribunal that they noticed that there was shooting coming from the house of Qani Jashari, what would be your comment on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. I have no comment to make. I was there myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As early as on that date, 10th of August, NLA members from Ljuboten were Rasim Murati, Faik Murati, Shefajet Bajrami, Besim Murtezani, Jetulla Arifi, Bekri Ajdini, Orhan Bajrami, Shefket Murati, Refedin Selimi, Feriz Selimi, at least these people were the members. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tenth one I didn't know. I stayed for six days at the hospital and then some of them came to visit me, but I didn't know this until the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering this new development and your concern what you should do, whether to leave the village or not, you stated that the crisis committee, Crisis Staff, told you to stay. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They said that the situation was coming down and that it was under control.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your family did not leave Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. No, we didn't left. No. On the 10th, when they told us not to leave our homes, not to panic because the situation then would calm down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But despite the suggestion of the crisis committee, some 50 families did leave Ljuboten on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left the crisis committee, I went to my house. I -- I met the -- I met my brother's wife. I was not married at that time, and then I don't know who left their houses or who didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Between the 10th and the 12th, did you receive information that families of Agim Jusufi, Kenan Jusufi, Sabit Jusufi, Rizah Alia, Vehaba Alia, Xhavid Alia, Afet Jashari, then the family of Rami Jusufi, his mother, wife, with the children, left the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask Your Honours that we move into private briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's comment, we ask for the counsel to read the names slowly for us and for the transcript

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the two of you that decided to go towards the forest and the woods came together to the house of Qani Jashari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Once you arrived in Qani Jashari's house, you found Qani Jashari there, Xhelal Bajrami, and Kadri and Bajram Jashari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in the house that was owned by Qani Jashari, in the house you found Qani Jashari, Xhelal Bajrami, and Kadri and Bajram Jashari. So you were six in total?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw there Kadri Jashari, Bajram and Xhelal and then we two, which makes five. I don't know if I saw anybody else because it was only two or three minutes. We heard then a big roar from Ahmeti's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask that the witness is shown 65 ter 1D88, page 1D1234.14, and in the Albanian version page 1D1254, and now P215 as a Prosecutor's exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At this page you recognise your signature, is that correct, because this is a statement that was shown to you by my learned colleague yesterday, which you gave on 10th of June, 2004?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct. It is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like, Your Honours, not to show this document and also not to show the other document that I'm about to show for the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The point 14 you have said: "When we entered Qani Jashari's house, Bajram Jashari, Kadri Jashari and Xhelal Jashari [sic] were already there. We were six persons in the house." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you go on saying in point 17. "All of us except Qani Jashari have left the room, and through the window we went towards the fields." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, except for I don't remember anything about Qani Jashari. I think he was not in the room when we went out, but together with the rest, we went to the -- toward the fields. It was -- we were panicked. So maybe I don't remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you would nevertheless agree that what you have said to the investigator of the Prosecutor in the statement that you corrected upon your arrival in The Hague and from what you testified today and yesterday before this Court, you would agree that there is a difference between the persons who were present in Qani Jashari's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me that there are certain discrepancies between what have you said in the statement that we have before us and which was given by you to the ICTY investigator and what you have said before there Court about who was present in Qani Jashari's house on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, I accept it and it is correct. But there are some elements that I don't remember about, because it was a terrible time then. Maybe it is the terror that has omitted some of the elements. These events took place in 2001. I think it's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In any event, you never saw Afet Jashari on that day, and he never came to Qani Jashari's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this. I stayed for only three, maximum five, minutes there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And before arriving in Qani Jashari's house, you knew that Afet Jashari, together with his family, has left the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to claim that those of you that were in Qani Jashari's house had automatic rifles and a Thomson, then you would agree with that claim. Would that be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you heard the police coming closer, as you testified, you got out or jumped out of the window and first you went towards the tobacco field and then through the meadows went to -- went towards the woods. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The first going out was Isa Zendeli, then it was Kadri Jashari, and then you were the one who got out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Xhelal and Kadri were behind you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was followed by Xhelal and Bajram. Kadri had already gone out and he was in the field. He was about half a metre in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I was confused, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He ran. He ran before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you started running from the tobacco fields through the meadows towards the forest, you were noticed from the army's position at Malistena; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's correct. Because when they shot at us, or, rather, when they shot at my direction, at the same time the hay -- we were covered by the hay and the soil, then the dust that the shots caused. Then Kadri was shot in his shoulder, and so it was a rain of bullets on us. I -- there is no way I can describe it. It was quite a terrible situation. It had never happened to me before. Then he was hit in his shoulder and in his back, and I don't know what else, because I don't know what to say. I didn't see him after that. So I don't know how many bullets hit him, but of course it was a big number of bullets.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also wounded from those positions, and you weren't able to assist Kadri. So with the hot wound you tried to reach the forest as soon as possible; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I looked back - I want to be clear - I saw that -- that he was hit by bullets and he also fell down. At the moment I felt a great heat in my leg and I looked down and I saw that blood was coming out, and I was not able to help him because there was also, there was this hail of bullets, as I mentioned, coming down on us, and I'm not sure about the types of weapons, because I did not go -- I did not do my military service, but in great haste I crawled away. I tried to hid myself from the bullets, because I would have been killed too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Only after arriving in the forest you were able to stop and then Isa Zendeli covered your wound with one of his T-shirts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Only then you were able to look towards Qani Jashari's house and then you saw that the roof of the house is on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Because after I tied the wound in my leg, I made for the -- for a certain place going toward the mountains where there are some oak trees and from when I left the window and to the oak trees, there are about 15 minutes. I think this is how long it took us. From the window to the oak woods, and then when Isa saw me, that I was -- that I was -- I had been wounded, he took his T-shirt and tied my legs and we looked back and we didn't look back to see the house, but we looked back to see whether we had been noticed. And at that moment we saw that the house was in fire, and I don't know what they set fire with.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You partially answered my next question. So neither you nor Isa Zendeli were not able to see nor you knew who and how set the house on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't see. I only saw the Hermelin car near the house when I was at the house, but then after that, I didn't -- I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in the house -- in the forest, I apologise -- actually, while you were walking through the woods towards Matejce, you were able to hear that from the area of the Matejce monastery where the NLA was -- that fire was opened towards the army positions, were you able to hear this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may only say that when we were trying to walk uphill, the Hermelin moved away from Jashari's house. This I saw with my own eyes. And whoever were responsible for that, they should know, and you may ask them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood, after you were helped and after your hospital treatment, you joined the NLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You joined the 114th Brigade, that was headquartered in Matejce; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was Brigade 114 but its base was in Nikustak. I was a member, but a member without a weapon, because in the meantime the Ohrid Framework Accord was signed so there was no need for me to have a weapon. Only the membership card.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My next question is exactly connected to your previous answer. Although you knew that the Ohrid agreements had been signed for over a month before your -- before you left the hospital, you continued to join some military groups; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not clear about the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: NLA was composed of persons -- of armed persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NLA had brigades and units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the framework agreement, all the NLA members had to disarm and to -- and the NLA was supposed to be dismantled; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true. And it is also a fact that they were disarmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But after you were released from the hospital over a month after the framework agreement had been signed, you joined an armed formation? Armed formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at the staff, but I know that. I know that the NLA was armed gradually unit by unit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Disarmed, correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I don't know when the last unit was disarmed. I know that first number 13, 12 and then 14 were disarmed. But I know that because I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you returned to the village, you never reported the event to the police of the Republic of Macedonia. You neither went to any prosecutor to tell what you know about the events; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then -- and later you had no trust to Macedonian police. You didn't want to talk to the police and you only gave your statements to the International Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. It was for security reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I hereby end with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. M-092. I am Jasmina Zivkovic and together with my colleague Antonio Apostolski, I appear on behalf of Mr. Johan Tarculovski. You told my learned colleague, you explained her how you went to Ljuboten on August 10th, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask if the witness could be shown photograph N005-7605.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-092, do you see this photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the fields on this photograph through which you walked from Radisani towards Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you zoom it in, please? I don't think I see the way I followed in this photo. I don't think this is the right photo. You have to show me the photo which shows the Radishan site when I got off the bus. It was a bus station in Radishan. Everybody knows where it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In the upper right corner --

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we ask to move the photograph to the left a little bit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this side here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A little bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't go that far. On the left, I think. More on the left. In the middle of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to help, to assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The usher will now give you the pen, Mr. M-092. Please mark the path.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you move the photo a little bit on the right, please? Please can you move the photo to its right side. No, no, not to the left; to the right. It's okay. It's not very clear to me. Now it's okay. There is like a tree grove when you enter the village. It's approximately the same route that I followed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And the path that you went through is two kilometres long, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because that place is close, one or two kilometres -- one kilometre from the house to the hill and from the hill to Radishan. I didn't measure it, of course, but it's approximately two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I tender this photograph as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 2D19, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-092, you said the shelling of the village of Ljuboten on Friday, 10th of August, started around 10.00 or 11.00 a.m.; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about August 10. Friday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shelling on Friday in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me first one more thing: At what time did you arrive to the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 9.00 I was in Stenkovac. I would say that around 12.00. It was a Friday, and I remember that the time for the Friday prayer was in an hour's time. So I know that I arrived in the village and prayed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So you can confirm that the shelling started on the 10th of August in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I heard some -- the noise of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: This means if someone were to state before this Court that the shelling on that day, the 10th of August, started around 8.00 in the morning, that someone would not be speaking the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. The truth is that when I arrived in the village from the city, there was nothing going on in the village. This is what I eye-witnessed. I'm not responsible for other people.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how many shells fell in the village of Ljuboten on the 10th of August, 2001? The Friday, let me clarify.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My house is at the school, near the school. They didn't fire the school or at my house, neither at Qenan Saliu's house they fell on a field. I saw two shells. Because my house is a little bit higher and the field lower and then I saw the dust rising from that field. But I know nothing about other shells.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And those two shells fell where in would you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the field. It was planted to wheat. I don't know, maybe they aimed at the houses, but they fell on the field. It is near the school, and near my own house.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said in your statement that you mainly spent -- spent the Friday inside your house, and the house of your relatives that is located near your house and that you never left for the field at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. We never left the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You spent most of the time on Saturday in the house of Shaban Zendeli and in the house of Afet Zendeli, and you still couldn't know what was happening in the village, considering that you stated that you couldn't see anything through the windows of the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were at the house of Shaban and Afet Zendeli, and we were inside. It is like kind of lower place, like a hole, because we felt more secure there. And of course we didn't see anything from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You told my learned colleague Ms. Residovic then that you were in the house of Shaban Zendeli, and then with Isa Zendeli you went to the house the Zendel Zendeli where you stayed for a short while,?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: For a very short while, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And after that you went to the house of Qani Jashari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now show the witness again the photograph N005-7603. Could you zoom the photo in. Not that much; a little bit less.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-092, in the photograph that you see in front of you, do you see the houses of Afet Zendeli -- no. I apologise, Shaban Zendeli, Zendel Zendeli?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the right photo. Show me the right photo, then I can indicate where they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move the photograph to the right --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see my house and the houses of my uncles. Just move it more. Stop it. Stop it. It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you now with the assistance of the usher to use the stylus --

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I apologise for the interruption. Perhaps this might be an appropriate moment to move into private session if there's going to be some marking and identification of homes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Today you told us that while you were running towards the forest, you were wounded -- your leg was wounded. My question is: From which side was your leg wounded, the front or the back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was lying down and a bullet hit me in my leg near my -- near my knee. Because at that moment bullets were falling. And I don't know what side I was looking at, because Kadri Jashari was hit at that time. And -- but the bullet did not hit my bone, so my bone was not broken.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You were shot at from the positions at Malistena.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From -- from the -- both from up and from down, from the Hermelin, because the bullets that hit Kadri Jashari did not come from Malistena position because he was hit in his back. There were a lot of bullets, and I don't know where the bullet that hit me came from, but I know --

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also explained that when you arrived to the forest, Isa Zendeli, when he arrived, bandaged your wound with a shirt, a T-shirt and you stay in the forest until a shepherd found you on Tuesday, the 14th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a T-shirt, yes. After Isa tied my wound with a T-shirt - it was a T-shirt because it was thin - we travelled for two days. The first day we walked, I slept the first night at someplace called Lajthia, and then I woke up in early morning. Then the second day, I woke up in the place called Ditaha [phoen] and then on Tuesday afternoon I took to walking again and we met a shepherd in Matejce mountains, somewhere there and he informed other people and called for help, because I was suffering -- I had been suffering from heavy bleeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So they took you to the Lipkovo hospital and then to the hospital at Nikustak; is that correct? So were in the military hospital at Nikustak. This is what you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I think I clarified things well, because Rexhep Selmani is a surgeon and in Lipkovo he was the one who cured my leg for five days, because Ridvan Bajrami does not have the right education or the education or the speciality of Rexhep who was the minister at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that you have stated that. I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now show the witness the document P218, and I ask that this document is not shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-092, you see the discharge note in front of you. In this medical discharge note, it is written that you were admitted at the hospital, you were hospitalised on the 12th of August, 2001, and that you were discharged on the 17th of September. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. Thank you for showing me this document, to make things more clear. Because yesterday I noticed that you could -- that you had some doubts with regard to this. On -- the 12th of August is the day when the event happened because they asked me what day that write there and I insisted on the day that I was wounded should have been written in the note. So that's why the date is there. That's the truth. You can also ask Mr. Rexhep Selmani and ask this question. That's the truth. This is the date when I was wounded, the 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that such data could possibly be written in your medical history file, but in the discharge note of any hospital there is always the admission date and the discharge date. These are the only data that are entered apart from the general basic data. That means, Mr. M-092, that on the 12th of August, 2001, you were in the military hospital in Nikustak, so that what you have stated that you were in Ljuboten on the 12th of August and then you were wounded, and then spent two days in the forest does not correspond with the written evidence, the discharge note, where it is written that that was the date that you were admitted at the hospital. Does it mean that you were wounded somewhere else and then taken to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true, that I was wounded somewhere else. Because I was really wounded. There is no other reason for me to be so sick. But I insisted on writing down the date when I was wounded, because I -- they didn't see me on the 12th. And it was Rexhep Selmani who took care of me personally. You can ask him personally. He is a well-known intellectual.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, considering that I will follow another direction of questions later, would this be with a good time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. And we resume at 4.15.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-092, we will go briefly back to the events from the Qani Jashari's house. You said that in front of the Qani Jashari's house gate you saw a Hermelin. What was the colour of the Hermelin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Green.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't know the answer to this question in 2004 when you were interviewed by the investigators.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drew a picture or a drawing of the Hermelin, also the -- the people coming out of the Hermelin, from its door. They were masked men. There was a Macedonian flag on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm about to ask you that. But at the question of the ICTY investigators in 2004 about the colour of the Hermelin you said that you don't remember, that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know now [as interpreted]. Now I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you saw two people in camouflage uniforms from the house at the very Hermelin to -- beside the Hermelin and six people leaving the back door to the Hermelin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: While in Qani Jashari's house, you said you only stayed there for just a few minutes. Did you or did anyone of the persons that you mentioned were together with you talked by some -- over some telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kadri Jashari, and he didn't hang up the phone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move briefly into a private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, once again, in what order did you leave the -- Qani Jashari's house through the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first one was Isa. And I don't remember well, because we first stopped at the place where there was some tobacco, but when we were running I know the order of the people, how we were running, but I don't remember -- I don't quite remember the order of getting out from the window. I remember that was Kadri, Isa, Xhelal Bajrami, we were all together, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That mean us that don't know what direction did Xhelal Bajrami and Bajram Jashari went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all together there at the place where tobacco was. But, as I said, I don't remember the order of people coming out from the window, who was the first one to get out of the window and the second. But I'm talking here about the skelja [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether I -- I didn't ask you whether you know the order but do you know what direction did Xhelal Bajrami and Bajram Jashari go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that, because up -- we went together to the place where the tobacco was. First was Isa, then Kadri and then me. But then I don't know what happened, because I couldn't see at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. As you say now, and as you already told my learned colleague today, in your escape towards the forest, you were frightened and you only thought how to reach the forest alive; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And that means, as you confirmed a while ago, that you weren't able to see what was going on with the others behind you. My question is: Does it mean that it might be possible that Kadri Jashari, Bajram Jashari and Xhelal Bajrami, that they have fired to the -- at the Macedonian security forces without you seeing that, as you have said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kadri Jashari was in front of me and what you said about him is -- it is not true. The police should -- you should consult this with the police and they will verify this what I'm saying. And I am talking here based on the attestations that I have given, and Kadri Jashari did not have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: But Bajram Jashari and Xhelal Bajrami, you didn't see them because they were behind you and you didn't look behind because you were fearing for your life, meaning that both -- the two of them could be firing without you seeing it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already mentioned that I went to Qani Jashari's house and I didn't see any weapons in their hands there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that the NLA fired with mortars towards the members of the security forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Isa was tying up the wound in my leg, I was trying to look if they were coming near us, to kill us, and in 2001, I'm talking, and they left immediately, the police. They left immediately, after the -- after the roof of the Qani's house caught fire, and when I arrived in Lipkovo they told me that they had fired at the direction of Ljubanci. That is true that they fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Could we briefly move into a private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-092, can you tell us, since you are a religious person, you have repeated this several times in the course of the questioning by my colleague Ms. Residovic. My question is whether as a hoxha, as a believer, could you join the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you be more explicit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does the religion allow you that you are a hoxha but also a member of a terrorist organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about terrorist organisation and I don't have the right to describe it as such. Second, if someone kills me, or if someone commits a massacre against you, when you don't feel free in the country you reside, then in these circumstances the religion allows you to do that, to defend your own home, or if the neighbour enters your home, then you have some right. I wanted to put it in a religious context, since you asked me that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Did you take an oath when you joined the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just took a photo, put on the uniform, and that's it. I was walking on crutches at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You told us also today that you joined NLA after the signing of the framework agreement. Can you tell us why did you join NLA then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They treated me. Rexhep Selmani was the first person who gave me help. Then we were killed, we were massacred. How couldn't I not join? If someone would fail under these circumstances to join then that is his own decision. Because we live side by side with the Macedonians. We sold our produce on the market side by side. We were on good relations with them. And the Macedonians know this very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, do you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will always remember what happened and you ask me why did you join. Of course I would join. That's why I'm here, to tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you understood well my question. My question is -- actually, I don't know whether I asked it well. My question is: Considering that the peace agreement was signed, what would be the reason for you to join it later? I could understand if you joined before that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we knew that the agreement was signed. But I went there and since I was admitted in their ranks I thought that maybe they would employ me somewhere like other people were. And further than that, I considered it a honour, like all Albanians did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So as far as I understand, you've spent a lot of time with those people from the NLA and I suppose you discussed the aims of the NLA with them. And considering all this, you then decided to join. Is it correct that the NLA fought for territories in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask the Court if we could move into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. You mentioned earlier that the NLA was disarmed at some point after the Ohrid agreement. Who gave the order to disarm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was given by KFOR or Ali Ahmeti. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you know who Ali Ahmeti was or is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you know if he holds a certain position and what is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a political leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In 2001, let's just make it more specific. In 2001, do you know what he was a political leader of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You also told us that you weren't given a weapon at the time that you joined the NLA. Were your colleagues at the time, other members of the NLA at that time that you joined, were they also not provided weapons or disarmed, that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw the soldiers there, they were armed. We were two persons, my cousin and myself. But after I was taken to hospital, I didn't see him anymore, but I know that my cousin and myself we didn't have weapons. But the other soldiers who were there for a longer time, they did have weapons. I don't know if I made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At some point, though, were the others that you were -- the others in your group, in that particular group of the NLA, were they at some point disarmed as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them were disarmed at a later time. All of them. All of them surrendered their weapons. When I had this photo taken, the soldiers stayed two or three more days. I don't remember the date. After I received this discharge note from the hospital, then I saw that there wasn't anyone armed in Nikustak, from 3, 4.000 soldiers that they used to be at least there is the approximate number I know. When I was released from hospital, they were about 50 left. When I went to Skopje, I don't think they were there anymore. At least this is what I know. Whether they stayed there more than two days or so, I don't know, because I went to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you were also asked about not reporting the events to the Macedonian police after they occurred. Were you ever contacted by any Macedonian authoritative body and/or the Macedonian police regarding the events that you have described to us today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But once I was in Gazi Baba neighbourhood and I saw them, but I don't think they came to contact me. Once I remember that they -- they called me to the Beko police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: My question to you was were you ever contacted by the Macedonian police or a Macedonian authoritative body regarding the events in Ljuboten that you've given us today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You also mentioned on page 45 of today's transcript Muzafer Agushi. And you indicated that he was wounded. Do you know where this person was wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above Basinec, I was told, and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We would thank you very much for the evidence you have given and for coming to The Hague. You will be pleased to know that that concludes the questions for you, and the court officer will show you out now and you will be free to leave and we would thank you once more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you, Your Honour, and we demand that justice prevail. We all look forward to justice outing, regarding what happened in Ljuboten and what I saw and what I heard about. Thank you very much indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Neuner will lead the next witness and I would respectfully like to remind the Court at a time that is convenient today may the Prosecution have a few minutes to address some of the issues that we discussed yesterday in private session. There was an issue related to protective measures that need to be addressed as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that conveniently dealt with now?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It could be, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I think we might do that and it might then be an appropriate time to have a break and then we can have an uninterrupted session with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I apologise. I'm searching for an e-mail that contains some information so I don't provide any misinformation to the Chamber. Are we in private session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're in public.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think, Mr. Saxon, before the next witness arrives it would be convenient to have the second break, and we will resume at 6.00 which will give us a complete hour with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is now given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, you have some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, witness?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your name is Mamut Ismaili?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And your ethnicity is Albanian?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You live in the village of Ljuboten in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I live in Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in October 2003 you provided a statement to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in April of this year, you met my colleague and myself in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And on that occasion you signed another statement containing this earlier statement from October 2003?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to take two statements, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ismaili, if you please look at the first statement with the ERN N006-4072 till 4077, and on the bottom of the first page, do you recognise your signature?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And of the entire document, did you sign each and every page?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could please help the witness to go to page 6 of that document. ERN is N006-4077.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the fields below "witness acknowledgment," do you recognise your signature here?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: No, I don't, this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the --

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, here, yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You looked at the upper of the two signatures on this page, for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If now the second statement could please be shown to Mr. Ismaili.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When we met in Ljuboten in April of this year, you had the opportunity to make corrections and addenda to your first statement that you have just seen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And all these additions and corrections were noted down in this second statement which is in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please confirm, looking at the first page, that the signature in the middle below is yours?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And after the statement had been read to you, did you have the opportunity to sign each page of this second statement?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we please, Mr. Usher, turn to page 7 of that second statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And it's the upper field where it says "witness declaration," do you find your signature here, Mr. Ismaili?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And together, does -- do both statements, the consolidated and the corrections, contain what you would say if would testify orally today in front of this Court?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question again, please, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I have shown you two statements now. And you stated that you had signed each of these two statements. If both statements would now be given to the Court would the content of both statements reflect what you would have said orally if would you have testified today in Court.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, can both statements he removed and I ask to tender both of them into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first statement will become Exhibit P219.1, and the second statement will become Exhibit P219.2, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will briefly summarize what is contained in the two statements. In the statements, the witness describes the shelling of Ljuboten in the time-period 10 till 12 August 2001, including the damage and destruction it caused. For example, two floors of the house of his father were damaged on the morning of 10 August 2001. Mr. Ismaili fled from Ljuboten on Sunday, the 12th of August, in the early afternoon towards Skopje with his family. They were stopped at Busolak [phoen] check-point by Macedonian police. Men were separated from women and children. The witness was ordered on the ground, to lie on the ground with approximately 50 other men. The police beat the detainees with rifle-butts, kicked them with boots and removed their personal possessions. The witness and other detainees were transferred first to Cair police station, then to Karpos police station and on Tuesday, 14 August, 2001, to Skopje Court II. At each location, the witness was beaten severely by police, at the Skopje Court II with rifle-butts and other objects. In court, the witness had to sign a document. Leaving this court, the witness was beaten again and transferred to Sutka prison. In September 2001, the witness and others were indicted for service in the enemy army. He was not convicted but pardoned and released after four months in detention in December 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ismaili, this is an accurate summary of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you now pictures. I want to take you to Friday morning, the 10th of August, 2001. In paragraph 3 of your consolidated statement you mentioned that you were in your father's house. And I wish to show you a photograph of Ljuboten with the ERN N005-7603.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If this could please be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you see the picture in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes. Can you zoom it in, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please point to the house of your father, or tell the cameraman if he has to move the camera, in which direction he has to move it.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: You have to move it on my left side. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, can the witness please be provided with a pointer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please point to the house of your father.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You encircle it already. Thank you. Could you mark a 1 next to this, please?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: This is it number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you describe in your statement that there was shelling coming from a location you mentioned referred to as Delba, could you point out where the shelling was coming from?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: They came from all sides, from here. It's a monastery here. It's on my left side. I think you have to move again the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we take this step by step, please. Can you first, when the picture is moved to the left, can you first point where the location Delba is?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Delba is on the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, we cannot technically move this photograph and contain the image that is being marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So if you want that, we need to receive that as an exhibit and then move to some other spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah. Then could you please sign the picture --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No need for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No need for that. So can we please retain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you want it received as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P220, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to say now which way you need the photo to be moved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On my right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we maybe zoom out a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: It's okay. Now I can see it. It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us on this larger image where is Delba?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you encircle this, please, this area Delba?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Shall I encircle it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: All this part is Delba.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And on that morning, the 10th of August, where do you believe that this shelling was coming from?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: From all sides. From Delba, Shulan [phoen], Kitka [phoen]. From all sides there were shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you're not sure from where exactly the shelling was coming from, which --

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: No, no. They came from all sides. I couldn't find out which direction they came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I please tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is the witness able to say whether either of Shulan or Kitka are to be seen on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, only Delba and a small part of Shulan can be seen here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you mark the small part of Shulan, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you put a number 2 against Shulan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For the record the witness has marked a number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On the Delba marking. And number 2 a part of Shulan. Do you tender that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, please. I ask to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P221, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You stated in paragraph 4 of your consolidated statement you saw burning houses in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you clarify, when did you see these houses burning?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: On Friday, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And this is the 10th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, the next picture --

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: No, excuse me, on Sunday. It was on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you provide the date, please?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: 10th of August -- 11 -- 12th August.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On Sunday, 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can please the photograph N005-7605 be shown to the witness. This could please be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Are you in a position to point out where the burning houses are -- were?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Should we zoom in a little bit more?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, but on the left side, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which direction you wish to go to? You said to the left side?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's okay now. Go on, go on. Again, again. A little bit more. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please encircle the houses which were burning on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Here are two houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Are these all houses which were burning?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: And another house was here. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And were you in a position to see what caused the burning?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: The Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Because the police had placed a check-point all around the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I please tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P222, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whose houses these are?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: They belonged to Sabit and Isuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Are we talking about last names or about first names here, with Sabit and Isuf?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Sabit and Isuf are first names. I don't know their last names.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I have one more photograph. The ERN is N004-4509; 65 ter number 199.21.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could this please be displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What do you recognise on this picture?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: On this picture, there was the police check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where was the police check-point, please?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Here. The main police check-point was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please encircle where you believe that the check-point was.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: The check-point was a little bit closer but you can't see it here. And here it was where they made us lie down on the ground. The women were separated from men. You can't see the check-point here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you just said you can't see the check-point but you also said you were --

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: You can't see it in the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You also said there was a location where you were asked to lay down. Can you encircle that place, please.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you know the name of this place?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Kodra e Zajmit [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is there another name for Kodra e Zajmit?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: I don't know. This is part of my field, my father's field, and we called it Kodra e Zajmit meaning Zajmi's hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where is the place where you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Here, the place where I encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P223, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Neuner. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Ismaili.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux, I'm appearing on behalf of Mr. Ljube Boskoski. You already told my learned colleague the Prosecutor about the basic data, about yourself, and I will just briefly ask you to confirm whether it's true that you were born on 30th of March, 1964 in Ljuboten and that you lived with your wife and your four children in Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You worked as a construction worker; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As my learned colleague already told you, you have given statements to the investigators of the ICTY. The first one that you gave was on the 28th and 29th of November, 2003; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You signed that statement, and then you stated that you have been telling the truth to the best of your recollection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the officer of the registrar of this Tribunal, on 20th of November, 2005, has certified that statement of yours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today my learned colleague the Prosecutor showed you the statement that you have given on the 23rd of April of this year in Ljuboten as a confirmation of the previously given statements and you also signed that statement. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the officer of the registrar, when he certified your statement in 2005 at that time you had the opportunity to see and read that statement in the Albanian language; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When, in Ljuboten, the officer of the Tribunal came to certify your previous statement on November 20th, 2005, at that time you got your statement in Albanian. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now when you gave this statement during the last month, in April 2007, you had an Albanian interpreter, and after he translated the statement you signed it in English. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't get the last statement in Albanian. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: It was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But since the interpreter was interpreting what was written down in the Albanian language, in respect what is in that statement you also signed it -- you signed the statement that was just been given -- shown to you by my colleague, whereby you say that everything that is written in the statement is the truth and that it has been told to the best of your recollection. Is that true that you have given such a statement that was shown to you today, that you have seen it and that you have signed it?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the statement was interpreted to you in Albanian, you wished to give a number of additions and changes to the -- to the so-given statement.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: That was about two weeks before coming to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then you gave numerous statements, clarifications, and amendments to your previous statement; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before providing these changes, the Prosecutor showed you various documents, which you commented and then you -- you provided additions and changes to them; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the comments that you gave, you signed personally; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ismaili, a while ago my learned colleague asked you about what you have heard and where was the sound of shelling coming from? That is to say, from what positions was Ljuboten shelled when you heard it for the first time? Do you remember being asked that? You remember then my colleague asked you could you tell us where was Ljuboten shelled from on 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: On the 10th of August, there was shooting from all over, from Delba, from Shulan. We couldn't even know, it was confusing. It was from all around the village, shooting and shelling. We couldn't identify because the shelling was coming from all over.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. That's what I understood. You answered the same to the questions of my colleague the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask that the witness is shown our document 65 ter 1D96, page 1D1350, which became Prosecutor's number P219.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you see at the bottom of this page your signature?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd ask also that the witness be shown 1D356 because that's the Macedonian translation so the witness -- he already has it, okay, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So that is the statement you have given and you have signed, 23rd of April, 2007 in Ljuboten. And in point 3 of your statement it said that it was on Friday, 10th of August, at 9.00 in the morning when the shelling of the village started from the place called Delba which is on the north side of the village. "I was in my father's house when the shell hit the first floor of his house." Is that written here?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it writes here, but we couldn't know whether it came from Delba, from Shulan. It came from all around. We couldn't identify the right side when the shelling. There was shelling from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your clarification. But at the question of my learned colleague you said, and you confirmed it to me as well, that on the 23rd of April, 2007 you gave a number of additions and changes to your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
