utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I ask that the witness is shown P290.2 -- P219.2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is also the statement that you saw a while ago and that you have signed. Is that true? And that was on the 23rd of April in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at that time you gave a large number of changes. That is, these changes were -- are presented in 12 points. I asked --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask that page that is our number 65 ter number 1D97, 1D1366. The same Prosecutor's number, but I don't know what page it is according to the Prosecutor's way of observing things, so it's easier for me to read the Defence number. That may be page 5 of the document, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can recognise your signature on this page. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as can you see in the third paragraph counted top down, you provided 12 paragraphs of changes to your previous statement, is that correct, that are contained in five pages of text?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you never mentioned nor you have provided any comment to point 3 whereby you said that on Friday, 10th of August, 2001, the shelling started from the place called Delba; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: I explained here before the shooting came from Delba, Shulan, Kitka, all around. Maybe there are mistakes in the changes. Maybe the translators made some errors, because I have noticed some errors in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Nevertheless, you could agree with me, that the statement that you gave today before the Court and the clarification that you have provided differs from what you have said in your previous statement. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, could I just draw your attention to paragraph 2, numbered 2, of the additions and corrections. I think it deals specifically with paragraph 3 of the original statement. Perhaps you've overlooked it. The last sentence may be relevant to what you're dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. Yes, there is a clarification different from the way that I asked the witness. I apologise. But it emerged from the direct examination and the way the witness insisted on the questions that my learned colleague asked. Maybe I did not make the right comparison, since that clarification was not as clear as what he said today, that the shooting came from all sides. Thank you, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ismaili, tell me, is it correct that the first statement on the events was given to the investigating judge of the Basic Court II in Skopje by you?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Can you please ask your question more explicitly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it correct that the first time you spoke about the events in Ljuboten on the 12th of August in your statement to the investigating judge of the Basic Court of Skopje II on the date, 14th of August, 2001, in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: They didn't ask. I just signed the text. I signed the text. They forced me to sign the text because of the ill-treatment, so -- I was bleeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you now show the witness 65 ter number 1D100, page 1D1384; and English 1D1386.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These are the minutes about the interrogation of a person on whom an investigation is started, and -- or requested and where it is written participants or present, the name of the investigating judge Jovan Lazarovski is written. Is that the judge who questioned you?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: I don't know him. He didn't introduce himself, what he was, a judge or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is your name written, name and last name written further in the text?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you look at this text here which contains various data, are the data noted here, the data related to you, and are they accurately entered here?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, they're accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask now that the second page of this document is shown. Macedonian 1D1385 and the English is 1D1387.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph here, it can be seen that you were informed about the right to speak in your own language and you stated that you spoke Macedonian language. Do you speak the Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, it was in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told the judge that you were unemployed and that you had no funds to pay for your attorney. Is it then correct that the court appointed an ex officio attorney, Ljubisa Dimitrov?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: I didn't have any attorneys. My lawyer came to meet only that night, but I wasn't assigned any attorneys. I didn't see any attorneys, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later your family chose another attorney for you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: On Sunday -- on Tuesday, they -- they sent a lawyer to me. I didn't know who sent him, but he said that his family sent me here to see whether you're alive or not. But then there was no more contact with the lawyer and there was no more need for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The judge then also cautioned you that you had the right to remain silent, that you are under no obligation to answer any questions and, as it is stated here, you said that you would not avail yourself of this right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Is it possible -- it is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You then described what you wanted to say to the judge, and then you stated -- you described how you came to the court, is that correct, and that you were not an NLA member?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Everything you stated, the court would say out loud and then the typist would enter it into the minutes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: They did not introduce themselves whether there was a registrar or a secretary. They just read out the statement, and I said that I hadn't done anything. And I told them that I had been beaten by the police and then they made me sign these statements. That was the thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You heard everything that the judge would say to this typist or the secretary as you're saying - I don't know what word you used - you listened, you heard everything that the judge dictated?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: It was a very small room. It wasn't any big courtroom. I only could understand that they sent me to prison for 30 days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But before they sent you to prison for 30 days, as you say, you had no objection on what the typist was writing or against what the judge was dictating for the record; is that correct? You never posed any objection?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, that's what happened. I told them that I was working in the Radishan, there are witnesses who could testify for that. But they didn't take any action to learn about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. From what you have read here now, you did not seek about any ill-treatment at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: I told the judge about the ill-treatment, about everything. Yes, I did. Yes, I did tell him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you left the remand prison after you were pardoned, you gave a statement to the representatives of the OSCE; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: I don't know about the OSCE. I gave a statement to NATO at the school. Yes, I -- I also gave statements to The Hague authorities but not to the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I would like to ask that the witness is shown 65 ter 1D98, Defence exhibit. The page is 1377. If we could zoom it in a bit so that the witness can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see under the number 15 that your name and last name are written here?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: The first name is not seen well here, but the last name, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe this first part of "Mamut" is not very legible. UT is legible.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: You can't see the M and the A from the first name there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, there is no other person by the name the Mamut Ismaili in Ljuboten. You are the only one.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is only me. Well, there are other people with this family name but with this first name, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask now that this witness is shown page number 1D1378, which should be the content of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, under the number noted here, you have given it to the representatives of the OSCE on the 10th of January, 2002. Do you remember that soon after new year 2002 you gave a statement to the representatives of the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wonder, Ms. Residovic, whether it would be convenient to pursue that tomorrow. If you're at a critical point, if you feel there is a question or two that you should put now you may, but we have reached the hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your indulgence, two questions to finish with this document so that we do not return to it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although you say you do not remember this document precisely, but as you can see it is in this document that you speak for the first time that this happened in the Butel police station, that there were you and six other inhabitants of Ljuboten, that your documents were reviewed again, et cetera, that some money were taken and it is written here that you were, in a way, ill-treated. At the bottom of this statement of yours where you have explained for the first time of having been ill-treated there is a note about the injuries provided by the representatives of the OSCE. It is stated here that you complain of pains in your knees and in your legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before the witness answers, the witness has said that he doesn't recognise having given a statement to the OSCE, and the statement -- the question just put to the witness is a kind of compound question as well. So if my learned colleague could maybe lay a foundation but the witness has said he doesn't recall having given such a statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness has recognised his name in the list of persons questioned by the OSCE and this is why I'm trying to refresh his memory using details from his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you will have to do it tomorrow. I know you were hoping to finish with the statement, but we're now well over time. Mr. Ismaili, we must finish now and we continue tomorrow at 2.15. I would ask you to return in time to continue your evidence then. We adjourn now for the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 24th day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.03 p.m.,
